scenes.title: simpligen
scenes.subtitle: VideoStudio · local AI video
scenes.narration: Welcome to simpligen VideoStudio. Every frame, voice, and picture in this video was made on one laptop, with no cloud and no API keys.

scenes.title: Write a scene file
scenes.subtitle: Title, narration, colours and an SVG diagram
scenes.narration: You describe the video as a short JSON file. Each scene has a title, a line of narration, and an optional SVG diagram.

scenes.title: Render locally
scenes.subtitle: Pillow draws, Kokoro speaks, ffmpeg encodes
scenes.narration: Pillow draws each slide and its diagram. Kokoro reads the narration. And ffmpeg times, fades, and encodes everything into an MP4.

scenes.title: Kokoro in Docker
scenes.subtitle: Natural voices, no API key, fully offline
scenes.narration: The voice you are hearing is Kokoro, an open weight speech model running in a local Docker container. If it is not running, simpligen falls back to the system voice.

scenes.title: What it costs
scenes.subtitle: $0 per render. Seconds of laptop CPU.
scenes.narration: There are no API keys and no per render fees. A one minute video costs a little laptop time and a fraction of a cent in electricity.

scenes.title: vs HyperFrames
scenes.subtitle: Two ways to make local video
scenes.narration: How does simpligen compare to HyperFrames from HeyGen? Both are free, open, and render locally with ffmpeg. HyperFrames turns HTML, CSS, and animation libraries into video through a headless Chrome browser, so anything a web page can draw, it can film. simpligen skips the browser: Python draws each frame, so it is tiny, fast, and easy to script.

scenes.title: Same intro, two ways
scenes.subtitle: Python frame loop vs HTML + GSAP timeline
scenes.narration: The animated intro you just saw is 161 lines of Python, and draws each 1080p frame in about 50 milliseconds. The same intro in HyperFrames is 58 lines of HTML, with an 11 line GSAP timeline. HyperFrames is shorter to write and far richer for motion design. simpligen needs no browser and no Node, and stays light enough to run next to the image model and the voice.

scenes.title: Local AI images
scenes.subtitle: Ollama writes the prompt, FLUX.2 Klein draws it
scenes.narration: The background pictures in this video were also made locally. A Gemma model in Ollama wrote each prompt, and FLUX.2 Klein, running through mflux, painted the image.

scenes.title: This video made itself
scenes.subtitle: python3 -m simpligen examples/demo.json
scenes.narration: This video, its animation, voice, and pictures were all generated by simpligen on one laptop, then deployed to Fly. Thanks for watching.
